questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was looking for courses that would fit into my chosen study track and would contribute something new to my curriculum. I also wanted to go somewhere where I have never been before and get to know a new culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was extremely easy to find information, the University of Melbourne was super helpful and they explained everything very clearly. It was also easy to get help from the university if something was unclear.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was picked up from the airport by a shuttle service organized by the university, which was very helpful. We also received a lot of information and guides during the welcome week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find campus housing, but we later found out that the same housing option was available directly from the organization for cheaper. It is also probably a lot cheaper to find housing by yourself but more stressful as well. It was good to know that the uni housing would be reliable, although it was really not clean (I lived at UniLodge Lincoln house). I do recommend it for meeting other students, I have met most of my friends in the dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived off campus but really near the campus (about a five minute walk), which was great because the Parkville campus is in the city center. So you are incredibly close to the city. I think it is also okay to live further, since I did not have many in person classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to register for courses through an online system, which mostly worked well and it was easy to use once you were familiar with it. First you had to pick the courses that you wanted to register for and then once registrations opened you could register in that portal. Then when they made the timetables available you had to check that your classes are not overlapping and potentially switch courses if there was a clash.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university offered help (Stop 1 and other services) when someone had issues with registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for my classes and did not have any clashes, so I could take all of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To check for the deadlines and have a back up in case there is a clash.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was expecting way way higher quality teaching.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were not really high quality, all of them were quite basic and simple. We also did not really have in person classes, for most courses I would have a one hour discussion session every week. Most people did not do readings outside of classes, which made the discussions also very superficial.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH I had way more contact hours during the week. In Melbourne I had a lot of free time and many group projects. The assignments were mostly essays in Melbourne and you had quite a lot of time to write them, with longer exam periods.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Women and Global Health, Comparative Health Systems, Social Determinants of Health Inequalities, International Policymaking in Practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None of the ones that I took because they were all very basic, maybe the Comparative Health Systems if you did not learn that much about health systems yet.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Using public transport was a lot more expensive than I thought

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive and transport also, drinks as well. Also flights were expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many options of activities, all sports clubs and other social clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was part of the film club which was very nice because they were screening a movie every week with free pizza. Also all of the exchange events were a lot of fun and you could meet many new people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really recommend the Great Ocean Road roadtrip, Tasmania and Sydney.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The local culture was really easy to adjust to, Melbourne is super easy-going and Australians are incredibly friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: All of the Australians are nice so don't be afraid to talk to them

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was hard to get used to people coming up to you and talking to you if you are from a culture where people are more reserved or private

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the friendliness and openness the most

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't expect incredible heat and sun because Melbourne is a bit cold, explore the city and its coffee culture, go out to the nature

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for many different accents in English, some of them being a bit hard to understand

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friends that I met here because I know that we will stay friends for life and we shared this crazy adventure

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The distance - both the time difference and the geographical distance, I felt really stuck sometimes and very homesick

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Melbourne is an incredible city

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
